No sensors on fbdarwin so i just commented out all sensor-related stuff
There's not even a RTC sensor?

Let's try using fbdarwin's dts for now, we can change it to the upstream one when it's ready:

https://github.com/facebook/openbmc/blob/helium/common/recipes-kernel/linux/6.12/0004-ARM-dts-aspeed-Add-Facebook-FBDarwin-AST2600-BMC.patch

I'm not really sure how to reference a downstream .dts file, from my understanding Yocto only knows to fetch .dts files from the github.com/torvalds/linux/tree/master/arch/arm/boot/dts/aspeed repo, so how should I reference this dts file ? can I do it locally?

Hi @robert3@meta.com, the .patch file adds the .dts file to the kernel source (see line 31-32, the `--- /dev/null` is a convention meaning that the file was added):

https://github.com/facebook/openbmc/blob/helium/common/recipes-kernel/linux/6.12/0004-ARM-dts-aspeed-Add-Facebook-FBDarwin-AST2600-BMC.patch#L31-L32

> can I do it locally?

Yes, TBH it might be cleaner to do this in our downstream repository for now
Yes, NICs in our FBOSS platforms are not connected through NCSI
I think it's a different baudrate for fbdarwin, right?
I think these stay the same ? (i.e. same ast2600)
Can we drop the "lf" prefix on this here?
Add a real description.  "initial commit for machine"?
Not sure what this refers to.  How can we "change" something in a new machine spec?

@patrick@stwcx.xyz So these files originate from the upstream yosemite5 skeleton. The commit message refers to the fact that I changed the baudrate and the bootargs inside recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot-aspeed-sdk/lfdarwin.cfg to fit darwin's machine specifications (i.e. CONFIG_BAUDRATE=9600 & CONFIG_BOOTARGS="console=ttyS0,9600n8 root=/dev/ram rw vmalloc=640M")

Please point this at something that is in the kernel tree then in the meantime.  Comment out this line until we get it done.

Need something other than `compute-...` here, since this isn't a compute system.  I suggest creating a new `facebook-network-device.inc` or `facebook-fboss.inc`.

@patrick@stwcx.xyz Removed the compute-singlehost include, trying to build an image without creating a new file inside openbmc/meta-facebook/conf/machine/include because I'm not really sure what should I add there yet.
I suspect you don't have an obvious use for these yet.  Leave them out and add them when you come up with a reason.

Please adjust your git-config to match your legal-ish name similar to what you see here: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1X-BqEwD6rlNVrlrXcH7vIHAawgo6lp8c/view?usp=drive_link .  (If you want to drop your middle name or last name or whatever, that's fine, just make sure it is recognizably similar to what is in the CLA).

`fb-fboss` should do instead?  If not, you'll need to let us know how bitbake is breaking.

Previously, bitbake was failing because it failed to fetch a server.ttyS2.conf file, so I had to create a new directory inside meta-facebook/recipes-phosphor/console/obmc-console/

Couldn't use configuration files in existing directories in that path because they were only for compute systems.

Tao mentioned it is not reliable to use ttyS* to reference a console since it is not reliable i.e. the index could be changed in the dts settings.

What device is used for host console logging in darwin? tty2 ? If yes, does the baudrate match ttyS0's i.e. 9600?

So bitbake stops complaining if the file is empty, so I'm just gonna leave it as it is right now since Tao suggested it's best that ttyS*.conf files should not reference a console because the index could be changed depending on the dts source.
